tagline: Pak Nam Pho, where the Chao Phraya River begins and the biggest Chinese New Year in Thailand happens
introHtml: Nakhon Sawan is a town a lot of people just drive through on the way up north, but it's actually the spot where the Ping, Wang, Yom, and Nan rivers all meet to become the Chao Phraya at a place called Pak Nam Pho, which is why locals call it the head of the Chao Phraya River. The town has a big Thai-Chinese community, so the Pak Nam Pho Chinese New Year festival is huge and lively enough that the whole country knows about it. Just outside town there's Bueng Boraphet, a large freshwater lake good for birdwatching, plus low hills like Khao No and Khao Kaeo with monkeys and caves, and Sawan Park right in the center where people come to walk and exercise morning and evening. It's a pass-through town that turns out to have more to see and eat than you'd expect if you actually stop.
bestTime: November–February, when the weather is cool and pleasant and birdwatching at Bueng Boraphet is at its best. Time it with Chinese New Year (January–February) for the Pak Nam Pho festival, the town's biggest event.

highlights.name: Pak Nam Pho, the head of the Chao Phraya River
highlights.blurb: The point where the Ping, Wang, Yom, and Nan rivers flow together to form the Chao Phraya. You can clearly see two different shades of water meeting — the signature image of Nakhon Sawan.

highlights.name: Pak Nam Pho Chinese New Year Festival
highlights.blurb: One of the biggest and oldest Chinese New Year festivals in Thailand, with processions carrying the city gods, dragons, and lions. People come from all over the country to watch.

highlights.name: Bueng Boraphet
highlights.blurb: The largest freshwater lake in Thailand and a haven for water birds and migratory species. Take a boat across the lake and catch a nice sunset.

highlights.name: Khao No–Khao Kaeo
highlights.blurb: Limestone hills along the Asia Highway with a troop of monkeys and a big cave underneath. A handy stop for photos and a quick visit to the temple along the way.

highlights.name: Sawan Park (Khao Kop)
highlights.blurb: A public park around a lake in the middle of town, with Khao Kop hill you can climb for city views and a lookout over the head of the Chao Phraya. Locals come here to walk and exercise.

highlights.name: Nakhon Sawan mochi
highlights.blurb: A well-known souvenir from the Chinese community at Pak Nam Pho — soft dough with all sorts of fillings, easy to pick up at shops around town.

foodScene.name: Kuai tiao pak mo (steamed rice-sheet noodles)
foodScene.note: Thin rice batter spread in a pot and wrapped around a filling — a popular breakfast around Pak Nam Pho, found at markets in town.

foodScene.name: Mochi
foodScene.note: The town's signature souvenir from the Chinese community: soft, chewy dough with bean, sesame, or custard fillings. Several shops in town to choose from.

foodScene.name: Pak Nam Pho Chinese restaurants
foodScene.note: An old Chinese town with dim sum spots, khao tom kui (rice congee with side dishes), and long-running Chinese restaurants worth trying.

foodScene.name: River fish and grilled fish
foodScene.note: Sitting on the Chao Phraya and next to Bueng Boraphet, the town has plenty of places for freshwater fish, grilled fish, and tom yum, all fresh.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha (Thai BBQ hotpot)
foodScene.note: A favorite dinner among locals, with plenty of spots to choose from at easygoing prices.

foodScene.name: Cafes in town
foodScene.note: The town center and riverside have several new cafes — a relaxed place to sip a coffee after a day of walking around.

foodScene.name: Pak Nam Pho market street food
foodScene.note: The old market quarter is full of snacks, sweets, and local dishes to graze on, and it gets especially busy during Chinese New Year.

foodScene.name: Stewed duck and khao man kai
foodScene.note: Chinese-style one-plate dishes you'll find all over town, with several long-established shops that have been at it for years.

attractions.name: Head of the Chao Phraya River, Pak Nam Pho
attractions.blurb: Where the Ping, Wang, Yom, and Nan rivers converge into the Chao Phraya, with a viewpoint and riverside dragon statues to stop and photograph.

attractions.name: Bueng Boraphet
attractions.blurb: The largest freshwater lake in Thailand and a spot for water birds and migratory species. Take a boat across the lake and watch the sunset.

attractions.name: Sawan Park (Khao Kop)
attractions.blurb: A public park around a lake in the middle of town, with Khao Kop hill for city views and the head of the Chao Phraya. Good for a morning or evening stroll.

attractions.name: Khao No–Khao Kaeo
attractions.blurb: Limestone hills along the Asia Highway with a troop of monkeys and a big cave underneath — a stop along the way up north.

attractions.name: Wat Khiriwong
attractions.blurb: A hilltop temple in the middle of town with the large white Phra Chulamani Chedi. Climb up to pay respects and take in views over Nakhon Sawan.

attractions.name: Pasan, the Chao Phraya Source Building
attractions.blurb: A curved landmark building set right at the river junction — a place to wander and take photos by the water in the heart of town.

attractions.name: Chao Pho Thepharak–Chao Mae Thapthim Shrine
attractions.blurb: An old shrine of the Pak Nam Pho community and the focal point of the procession during Chinese New Year every year.

attractions.name: Hat Sai Ngam (Wat Khao No–Wang Rom Klao Dam)
attractions.blurb: A riverside spot to relax out in the rural part of the province, good for taking in the scenery and the water depending on the season.
